focus: The cold first prompt: measured load versus waiting bounds
noveltyJustification: Four of five findings compose new bounds from four files; the fifth restates the unavailable-row gap.

Treating 2,500 ms as the cold cost (it is the cascade probe ceiling)

graphEvents.label: Measured cold work is about 690 ms against a 2,500 ms hook budget
Cascade probe default 2,500 ms can consume the whole hook budget
CLI cold wait and local scorer deadline are 5,000 ms, twice the caller budget

label: The measured cold work is about 690 ms (271-277 ms cold embedding plus 413 ms cold advisor CLI), 27.6 percent of the 2,500 ms Claude hook budget.
The cascade probe default of 2,500 ms equals the Claude shim's child kill at 2,500 ms, so a probe that runs to its default leaves no time for scoring and fails open.

Both server-side cold waits are 5,000 ms (COLD_START_WAIT_MS and LOCAL_SCORER_TIMEOUT_MS), twice the 2,500 ms caller budget, so a path that honours its own wait can only be observed as a caller timeout.
The 664 unavailable health rows price a cold fail-open at p50 0 ms and p95 2 ms, so the population that should carry the cold cost carries none of it.
What would confirm the bound: one sandbox cold start with the embed model unloaded, recording hook wall time, cascade probe duration and fail-open reason.
